original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-explain-condition}
Let $A \to B$ be a map of Noetherian rings. Consider the conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item nonzerodivisors of $A$ map to nonzerodivisors of $B$,
\item (1) holds and $Q(A) \to Q(A) \otimes_A B$ is flat,
\item $A \to B_\mathfrak q$ is flat for every
$\mathfrak q \in \text{Ass}(B)$,
\item (3) holds and $A \to B_\mathfrak q$ is flat for every $\mathfrak q$
lying over an element in $\text{Ass}(A)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we have the following implications
$$
\xymatrix{
(1) & (2) \ar@{=>}[l] \ar@{=>}[d] \\
(3) \ar@{=>}[u] & (4) \ar@{=>}[l]
}
$$
If going up holds for $A \to B$ then (2) and (4) are equivalent.
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings and put $K=Q(A)=S^{-1}A$ where $S$ is the multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors of $A$. Write $\operatorname{Ass}_R(R)$ for the set of associated prime ideals of a Noetherian ring $R$. Consider: (1) every element of $S$ maps to a nonzerodivisor of $B$; (2) (1) holds and $K\to K\otimes_AB$ is flat; (3) for every $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(B)$, the map $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat; (4) (3) holds and $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat for *every* $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ contracting to a member of $\operatorname{Ass}_A(A)$. Then (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), (2)$\Rightarrow$(4), (4)$\Rightarrow$(3), and (3)$\Rightarrow$(1). If $A\to B$ also satisfies going up (every chain of primes of $A$ lying above the contraction of a prime of $B$ can be lifted to a chain of primes in $B$ beginning at that prime), then (4)$\Rightarrow$(2) as well; hence (2) and (4) are equivalent under going up. No other implications are asserted.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-agree-dedekind}
Assume the Dedekind different is defined for $A \to B$.
Set $X = \Spec(A)$ and $Y = \Spec(B)$. The generalization of
Remark \ref{remark-different-generalization}
applies to the morphism $f : Y \to X$ if and only if
$1 \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$ (e.g., if $A$ is normal, see
Lemma \ref{lemma-dedekind-different-ideal}).
In this case $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ is an ideal of $B$ and we have
$$
\mathfrak{D}_f = \widetilde{\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}}
$$
as coherent ideal sheaves on $Y$.
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite map of Noetherian rings such that every nonzerodivisor on $A$ maps to a nonzerodivisor on $B$. Put $K=Q(A)$, the total quotient ring obtained by inverting all nonzerodivisors of $A$, and $L=B\otimes_AK$. Assume $K\to L$ is finite étale; these conditions mean the *Dedekind different is defined*. Put $\mathcal L_{B/A}=\{z\in L:\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(bz)\in A\text{ for every }b\in B\}$ and $\mathfrak D^{\mathrm D}_{B/A}=\{z\in L:z\mathcal L_{B/A}\subseteq B\}$. The complementary module has the canonical trace-pairing identification $\mathcal L_{B/A}\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,A)=\omega_{B/A}$. Let $f:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the induced finite quasi-finite morphism. The conditions for the generalized relative different to be defined are precisely: the flat locus of $f$ contains $\operatorname{Ass}(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B})$ and the inverse image of $\operatorname{Ass}(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A})$, and its trace section on that flat locus extends to a global section of $\omega_{B/A}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,A)$. These conditions hold *if and only if* $1\in\mathcal L_{B/A}$ (which in particular holds if $A$ is normal). In that case the extension is the functional $b\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(b)$, the Dedekind different is an actual ideal of $B$, and the generalized different on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ equals its associated coherent ideal sheaf: $\mathfrak D_f=\widetilde{\mathfrak D^{\mathrm D}_{B/A}}$. This equality need not diagnose ramification in non-flat cases.

\label{lemma-compare-dualizing}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a quasi-finite separated morphism of Noetherian schemes.
For every pair of affine opens $\Spec(B) = V \subset Y$,
$\Spec(A) = U \subset X$ with $f(V) \subset U$ there is an isomorphism
$$
H^0(V, f^!\mathcal{O}_X) = \omega_{B/A}
$$
where $f^!$ is as in
Duality for Schemes, Section \ref{duality-section-upper-shriek}.
These isomorphisms are compatible with restriction maps and define a canonical
isomorphism $H^0(f^!\mathcal{O}_X) = \omega_{Y/X}$ with
$\omega_{Y/X}$ as in Remark \ref{remark-relative-dualizing-for-quasi-finite}.
Similarly, if $f : Y \to X$ is a quasi-finite morphism of schemes of
finite type over a Noetherian base $S$ endowed with a dualizing complex
$\omega_S^\bullet$, then $H^0(f_{new}^!\mathcal{O}_X) = \omega_{Y/X}$.

\label{lemma-compare-trace}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a finite flat morphism of Noetherian schemes.
The map
$$
\text{Trace}_f : f_*\mathcal{O}_Y \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_X
$$
of Section \ref{section-discriminant}
corresponds to a map $\mathcal{O}_Y \to f^!\mathcal{O}_X$ (see proof).
Denote $\tau_{Y/X} \in H^0(Y, f^!\mathcal{O}_X)$ the image of $1$.
Via the isomorphism $H^0(f^!\mathcal{O}_X) = \omega_{X/Y}$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-compare-dualizing}
this agrees with the construction in
Remark \ref{remark-relative-dualizing-for-flat-quasi-finite}.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gorenstein-quasi-finite}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein,
\item $f$ is flat and the fibres of $f$ are Gorenstein,
\item $f$ is flat and $\omega_{Y/X}$ is invertible
(Remark \ref{remark-relative-dualizing-for-quasi-finite}),
\item for every $y \in Y$ there are affine opens
$y \in V = \Spec(B) \subset Y$, $U = \Spec(A) \subset X$
with $f(V) \subset U$ such that $A \to B$ is flat
and $\omega_{B/A}$ is an invertible $B$-module.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes. For an affine map of Noetherian rings $A\to B$ arising locally from $f$, define $\omega_{B/A}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,A)\otimes_EB$ using a finite $A$-algebra $E$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is an open immersion, and let $\omega_{Y/X}$ be the coherent sheaf formed by gluing these modules. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is a Gorenstein morphism; (2) $f$ is flat and every scheme-theoretic fibre is Gorenstein (equivalently, its local rings are Gorenstein); (3) $f$ is flat and $\omega_{Y/X}$ is an invertible sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules; (4) for every $y\in Y$ there are affine opens $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(V)\subseteq U$, such that $A\to B$ is flat and $\omega_{B/A}$ is invertible as a $B$-module. The invertibility requirement is that the relative dualizing module be locally free of rank one, not merely that it be flat.

conclusions: Gorensteinness, flatness with Gorenstein fibres, and invertibility of the relative dualizing module (globally/affine locally) are equivalent.
